biography: Helen Nissenbaum is a philosopher of technology and information scientist known for work on privacy, bias, accountability, and the social values built into technical systems. Her theory of contextual integrity treats privacy as appropriate information flow rather than secrecy alone: data practices must be judged against the purposes, roles, and norms of the context in which information moves. Her work helps PHIL 123 follow responsibility through systems whose categories, handoffs, and institutional uses can obscure who has power and who must answer.

teaching.whyThisPerson: Nissenbaum supplies tools for judging when data crosses contexts, how bias enters systems, and why computerized decisions remain answerable to human norms.
